'''Matthias Werner Hentze''' (born 25 January 1960) is a German scientist. He is the Director of the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]] (EMBL).<ref name="EMBL Leadership">{{Cite web |title=Matthias Hentze |url=https://www.embl.org/people/person/hentze/ |website=EMBL |access-date=26 September 2023}}</ref> and co-founder of the [[Molecular Medicine Partnership Unit]] (MMPU).<ref name="j715">{{cite web | title=Biography | website=EMBL.org | url=https://www.embl.org/governance/director/biography/ | access-date=17 November 2025}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Matthias Hentze studied medicine in the UK at the [[Medical school in the United Kingdom|medical schools]] at the universities of [[Southampton]], [[Oxford]], Glasgow and [[Cambridge]], and in Germany at the [[Westfälische Wilhelms-Universität]], [[Münster]] from which he qualified in 1984.<ref name="Leopoldina CV" /> In the same year, he received his [[Doctor of Medicine|M.D.]] degree for a dissertation on the role of [[glycosylation]] in lysosomal enzyme expression with Kurt von Figura as his advisor.<ref name="Leopoldina CV">[http://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Hentze_Matthias_EN.pdf Leopoldina CV. Retrieved 2020-07-30.]</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1= Hentze |first1= M. |last2= Hasilik |first2= A. |last3= Figura |first3= Kurt v. |title= Enhanced degradation of Cathepsin D synthesized in the presence of the threonine analog beta-hydroxynorvaline | journal= Arch. Biochem. Biophys. |volume= 230 |issue= 1 |pages= 375–82 |pmid= 6424571 |doi=10.1016/0003-9861(84)90120-6 |year=1984}} Retrieved 6 August 2015.</ref>

After a short phase of clinical work, Hentze became a postdoctoral fellow at the [[NIH|National Institutes of Health]] (Bethesda, Maryland, USA) in 1985, having been awarded a fellowship by the [[German Research Foundation]] ([[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|DFG]]).<ref name="Leopoldina CV" />{{better source needed|date=February 2023}} In 1989, he joined the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]] in Heidelberg as an independent group leader.{{citation needed|date=July 2025}} In 1990, he obtained the ''[[Habilitation]]'' from the [[Heidelberg University|Ruprecht-Karls University]] in Heidelberg and was appointed Dean of the EMBL International Ph.D. Programme in 1996.<ref name="Leopoldina CV" />

==Career==
Since 1996, Hentze has held positions in EMBL's scientific administration, initially as Dean of the EMBL International PhD Programme<ref>{{Cite web |title=Training: EMBL International PhD Programme |url=http://www.embl.de/training/phdprogramme/index.html |website=EMBL |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041209235146/http://www.embl.de/training/phdprogramme/index.html |archive-date=9 December 2004}}</ref> and in the establishment and expansion of EMBL's internal and external training programs. He played a key role in the conceptualisation and establishment of the Advanced Training Centre (ATC) in Heidelberg.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Smaglik |first=Paul |title=EMBL offers lab training in Europe |journal=Nature |volume=457 |number=7233 |page=1172 |date=26 February 2009 |doi=10.1038/nj7233-1172b|doi-access=free }}</ref> He has also overseen the development of EMBL's fundraising and alumni programs, and established EMBL's first Bioethics Committee, which he chaired from 2004 to 2020.<ref name="Leopoldina CV" />

Together with Andreas Kulozik of the Medical Faculty of Heidelberg University, Hentze co-founded the [[Molecular Medicine Partnership Unit]] (MMPU) in 2002<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Smaglik|first1=Paul|s2cid=4416590|title=Language lessons: Heidelberg.|journal=Nature|date=15 May 2003|volume=423|issue=6937|pages=364–5|pmid=12748657|doi=10.1038/nj6937-364a}}</ref><ref>{{Cite press release |date=18 July 2005|title=Molecular Medicine Partnership Unit initiates second phase|url=https://www.embl.org/news/lab-matters/molecular-medicine-partnership-unit-initiates-second-phase/|access-date=26 September 2023|website=EMBL}}</ref> and served as its co-director until May 2025.<ref name="Leopoldina CV" />

In 2005, Hentze became Associate Director of the EMBL and Professor for Molecular Medicine at the [[University of Heidelberg]].<ref name="Leopoldina CV" /> In 2013, Hentze was appointed Director of EMBL.<ref name="EMBL Leadership" />

Hentze founded the Environmental Research Initiative (ERI) in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About EMBL |url=https://www.embl.de/aboutus/support-embl/what-to-support/environmental-research-initiative/ |website=EMBL |access-date=21 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210611095555/https://www.embl.de/aboutus/support-embl/what-to-support/environmental-research-initiative/ |archive-date=11 June 2021}}</ref> ERI connects private donors with the scientific potential of researchers at EMBL.{{citation needed|date=July 2025}}

Hentze serves or served on the editorial boards of Molecular Cell, ''RNA'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editors, Editorial Board and Coordinators for ''RNA'' |url=https://rnajournal.cshlp.org/site/misc/edboard.xhtml |website=RNA Journal |access-date=26 September 2023}}</ref> ''EMBO Molecular Medicine'',<ref>[http://d3gz45kfcn01zz.cloudfront.net/editors#seniored EMBO Press – Editors & Advisory Editorial Board. Retrieved 2015-07-20.]</ref> ''Trends in Biochemical Sciences'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Advisory board: Trends in Biochemical Sciences|url=https://www.cell.com/trends/biochemical-sciences/advisory-board|access-date=26 September 2023|website=Cell Press}}</ref> ''Journal of Molecular Medicine'',<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.springer.com/biomed/molecular/journal/109/PSE?detailsPage=editorialBoard |title=Editorial Board |access-date=20 July 2015 |website=Journal of Molecular Medicine |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924120150/https://www.springer.com/biomed/molecular/journal/109/PSE?detailsPage=editorialBoard |archive-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> ''BMC Molecular Biology'',<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.biomedcentral.com/bmcmolbiol/about/edboard |title=Editorial Board |website=BMC Molecular Biology |access-date=20 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150720224328/http://www.biomedcentral.com/bmcmolbiol/about/edboard |archive-date=20 July 2015}}</ref> and ''Wiley Interdisciplinary Reviews: RNA''.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1002/wrna.1275 | volume=6 | issue=1 | title=Issue information | year=2014 | journal=Wiley Interdisciplinary Reviews: RNA| article-number=wrna.1275 | s2cid=222188869 }}</ref>

Hentze is or was a member of the Scientific Advisory Board and Board of Trustees of the Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine<ref>[https://www.mdc-berlin.de/system/files/migrated_files/fiona/MDC_research_report_2014.pdf MDC Research Report 2014. Page 321. Retrieved 2020-07-30.]</ref> (Berlin, Germany), the scientific advisory board of the [[Berlin Institute of Health]] (BIH/BIG),<ref>{{Cite press release |title=Berliner Institut für Gesundheitsforschung startet erste Forschungsprojekte // Prof. Dr. Jörg Hacker, Präsident der Leopoldina, zum Vorsitzenden des Wissenschaftlichen Beirats gewählt |url=https://www.mdc-berlin.de/de/news/archive/2014/20140312-berliner_institut_f_r_gesundheitsforschung |date=12 March 2014 |access-date=26 September 2023 |publisher=Max Delbrück Center (MDC) |language=de}}</ref> the Istituto Nazionale Genetica Molecolare (INGM), Milan, Italy,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scientific Advisory Board |url=https://ingm.org/en/scientific-advisory-b/ |website=Istituto Nazionale Genetica Molecolare (INGM) |access-date=26 September 2023}}</ref> the Centenary Institute, Sydney, Australia,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scientific Advisory Board |url=https://www.centenary.org.au/about/governance/scientific-advisory-board/ |website=Centenary Institute |access-date=26 September 2023}}</ref> the [[King Abdullah University of Science and Technology|KAUST]] Center for Smart Health, the International Scientific Advisory Board (ISAB) "RNA for Therapy", CEITEC, Brno, Czech Republic,<ref>{{cite web | title=International Scientific Board | url=https://www.uochb.cz/en/rna4t-board }}</ref> and the Cold Spring Harbor Conferences Asia.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.csh-asia.org/?about/57 |title=Overview & SAB |website=Cold Spring Harbor Asia |access-date=26 September 2023}}</ref> Furthermore, Hentze is the scientific co-founder of Anadys Pharmaceuticals, San Diego, USA.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://talks.ox.ac.uk/talks/id/ff9d4366-e304-4d87-a31d-c3dfd78bc78a/ |title=Hidden treasures of the RNA World: from moonlighting to riboregulation |website=Oxford Talks |publisher=University of Oxford |date=2019 |access-date=26 September 2023}}</ref>

== Research ==
Hentze's research focuses on [[RNA]] biology and [[RNA-binding protein]]s. In 1987, Hentze and his colleagues discovered [[iron-responsive element]]s as first example of an RNA element regulating the [[Translation (biology)|translation]] of mammalian [[Messenger RNA|mRNA]] into proteins.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hentze |first1=MW | last2=Caughman |first2=SW |last3=Rouault |first3=TA |last4=Barriocanal |first4=JG |last5=Dancis |first5=A |last6=Harford |first6=JB |last7=Klausner |first7=RD |title=Identification of the iron-responsive element for the translational regulation of human ferritin mRNA |journal=Science |volume=238 |issue=4833 |pages=1570–73 |date=1987 |pmid=3685996 |doi=10.1126/science.3685996|bibcode=1987Sci...238.1570H |url=https://zenodo.org/record/1231213 }}</ref> Hentze's research group has paved the way for understanding translational control ([[RNA-binding protein|RNA-binding proteins]], [[MicroRNA|microRNAs]]) whose significance for developmental biology, brain function, carcinogenesis and other diseases has in the meantime become widely recognized.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sonenberg |first1=N | last2=Hinnebusch |first2=A |title=New modes of translational control in development, behavior, and disease |journal=Mol Cell |volume=28 |issue=5 |pages=721–29 |date=14 December 2007 |pmid=18082597 |doi=10.1016/j.molcel.2007.11.018|doi-access=free |url=http://escholarship.mcgill.ca/downloads/sf268b51n |hdl=20.500.14905/76755 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> Moreover, he has made key discoveries in the area of iron metabolism and disease.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hentze |first1=MW | last2=Muckenthaler |first2=MU |last3=Galy |first3=B |last4=Camaschella |first4=C |s2cid=23971474 |title=Two to tango: regulation of mammalian iron metabolism |journal=Cell |volume=142 |issue=1 |pages=24–38 |date=9 July 2010 |pmid=20603012 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2010.06.028|doi-access=free |bibcode=2010Cell..142...24H }}</ref>

In 2010, Hentze proposed the concept of REM Networks, a new interconnection between metabolism and gene expression on the basis of RNA-binding proteins.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hentze |first1=MW | last2=Preiss |first2=T |title=The REM phase of gene regulation |journal=Trends Biochem Sci |volume=35 |issue=8 |pages=423–26 |date=2010 |pmid=20554447 |doi=10.1016/j.tibs.2010.05.009}}</ref> The research project was awarded the ERC Advanced Investigator Grant by the [[European Research Council]] in 2011.<ref name="ERC">[https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/294298 Exploring the interface between cell metabolism and gene regulation: from mRNA interactomes to "REM Networks"]. European Commission/CORDIS EU Research results. Retrieved 29 July 2020.</ref> Work following this hypothesis led to the development of the "RNA Interactome Capture" technique and to the discovery of hundreds of formerly unknown RNA-binding proteins in the cells of living organisms from human to yeast, including more than 100 metabolic enzymes.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Castello |first1=A | last2=Fischer |first2=B |last3=Schuschke |first3=K |last4=Horos |first4=R | last5=Beckmann |first5=BM |last6=Strein |first6=C | last7=Davey |first7=NE |last8=Humphreys |first8=DT |last9=Preiss |first9=T |last10=Steinmetz |first10=LM |last11=Krijgsveld |first11=J |last12=Hentze |first12=MW |s2cid=17912260 |title=Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins |journal=Cell |volume=149 |issue=6 |pages=1393–1406 |date=8 June 2016 |pmid=22658674 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2012.04.031|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Beckmann |first1=BM | last2=Horos |first2=R |last3=Fischer |first3=B |last4=Castello |first4=A |last5=Eichelbaum |first5=K |last6=Alleaume |first6=AM |last7=Schwarzl |first7=T |last8=Curk |first8=T |last9=Foehr |first9=S |last10=Huber |first10=W |last11=Krijgsveld |first11=J |last12=Hentze |first12=MW |title=The RNA-binding proteomes from yeast to man harbor conserved enigmRBPs |journal=  Nature Communications|volume=6 |issue=1012 |date=3 December 2015 |article-number=10127 |pmid=26632259 |doi=10.1038/ncomms10127 |doi-access=free|pmc=4686815 |bibcode=2015NatCo...610127B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hentze |first1=MW | last2=Castello |first2=A |last3=Schwarzl |first3=T |last4=Preiss |first4=T |s2cid=4938952 |title=A brave new world of RNA-binding proteins |journal=Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol |volume=19 |issue=5 |pages=327–41 |date=17 January 2018 |pmid=29339797 |doi=10.1038/nrm.2017.130|bibcode=2018NRMCB..19..327H |url=http://eprints.gla.ac.uk/219002/1/219002.pdf }}</ref> Hentze and his colleagues also discovered new RNA-binding motives of proteins which they unraveled using the newly developed method called "RBDmap".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Castello |first1=A | last2=Fischer |first2=B |last3=Frese |first3=CK |last4=Horos |first4=R |last5=Alleaume |first5=AM |last6=Foehr |first6=S |last7=Curk |first7=T |last8=Krijgsveld |first8=J |last9=Hentze |first9=MW |title=Comprehensive identification of RNA-binding domains in human cells |journal=Mol. Cell |volume=63 |issue=4 |date=18 August 2016 |pages=696–710 |pmid=27453046 |doi=10.1016/j.molcel.2016.06.029|pmc=5003815 }}</ref>

In 2019, they described the concept of riboregulation. They found out that the autophagy receptor protein [[Nucleoporin 62|p62]] is directly regulated by a small RNA, vtRNA1-1, and that the small RNA directly interferes with protein-protein interactions between p62 monomers.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Horos |first1=R | last2=Büscher |first2=M |last3=Kleinendorst |first3=R |last4=Alleaume |first4=AM |last5=Tarafder |first5=AK |last6=Schwarzl |first6=T |last7=Dziuba |first7=D |last8=Tischer |first8=C |last9=Zielonka |first9=EM |last10=Adak |first10=A |last11=Castello |first11=A |last12=Huber |first12=W |last13=Sachse |first13=C |last14=Hentze |first14=MW |s2cid=72333202 |title=The Small Non-coding Vault RNA1-1 Acts as a Riboregulator of Autophagy |journal=Cell |volume=176 |issue=5 |pages=1054–67 |date=21 February 2019 |pmid=30773316 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2019.01.030|doi-access=free |url=https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/222056/1/222056.pdf }}</ref> They reported a new form of riboregulation in 2022: RNA binds to the catalytic center of the human enzyme enolase-1 and inhibits its glycolytic activity.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Huppertz |first1=Ina |last2=Perez-Perri |first2=Joel I. |last3=Mantas |first3=Panagiotis |last4=Sekaran |first4=Thileepan |last5=Schwarzl |first5=Thomas |last6=Russo |first6=Francesco |last7=Ferring-Appel |first7=Dunja |last8=Koskova |first8=Zuzana |last9=Dimitrova-Paternoga |first9=Lyudmila |last10=Kafkia |first10=Eleni |last11=Hennig |first11=Janosch |last12=Neveu |first12=Pierre A. |last13=Patil |first13=Kiran |last14=Hentze |first14=Matthias W. |date=21 July 2022 |title=Riboregulation of Enolase 1 activity controls glycolysis and embryonic stem cell differentiation |url=https://www.biorxiv.org/content/biorxiv/early/2020/10/14/2020.10.14.337444.full.pdf |journal=Molecular Cell |language=en |volume=82 |issue=14 |pages=2666–2680.e11 |doi=10.1016/j.molcel.2022.05.019 |pmid=35709751 |s2cid=249722068 |issn=1097-2765|doi-access=free }}</ref> Currently, their research focuses on how widely biological processes are riboregulated, and how riboregulation determines cell metabolism, differentiation and malignant processes.

Hentze is (co-)author of textbooks about Molecular Medicine and has published over 300 scientific original contributions.<ref name="Leopoldina CV" />
